Answer: F
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates bronchiectatic changes (tram-tracking, ring shadows) that are bilateral but more pronounced in the left lower lobe. In Kartagener's syndrome with situs inversus totalis, the morphological right lung is located on the left side; since bronchiectasis typically affects the middle and lower lobes of the morphological right lung, this finding is consistent with the expected presentation.
